name: Enterprise Project Bid Presentation
description: A formal oral-defense bid deck in white, deep navy, and muted gold, mapping RFP requirements to a certified solution, execution team, risk controls, commercial value, SLAs, and binding commitments.
style_guide:
# Enterprise Project Bid Presentation

## Purpose

Create a formal oral-defense presentation that makes compliance, solution fit, delivery capability, risk control, and commercial accountability easy to evaluate. The deck must map stated RFP criteria to a specific response and supporting evidence. It is not a general company capabilities deck or an opportunity pitch. Preview clients, RFP IDs, certifications, personnel, performance, savings, SLAs, and guarantees are fictional.

## Visual signature

Use a persistent deep-navy stage rail at left, a white main evidence field, and muted gold for requirement IDs, certification, selected proof, and commercial emphasis. High-contrast serif titles convey formality; neutral sans-serif supports technical evidence; mono labels make requirements and stages traceable. The system resembles a controlled bid document adapted for oral defense.

## Canvas and layout

- Fixed 16:9 canvas with a left rail occupying `17–19 percent` of width and a main content field with `55–75 px` internal margins.
- The rail carries stage number, stage title, and one-sentence purpose. It remains consistent on pages 2–6.
- Main area uses three requirement cards, `8/4` solution-and-moat split, stacked timeline and team panels, a full-width risk table, or three commercial KPI cards plus commitment band.
- Cards are square, thin-bordered, and shadowless.
- Maintain enough space for evaluators to scan requirement IDs and evidence quickly.

## Colors

- Bid navy `#091D43`: cover split, stage rail, headers, commitments, and authority.
- Muted gold `#C9A255`: requirement highlight, stage code, certification, selected value, and divider.
- White `#FFFFFF`: dominant evidence field.
- Cool off-white `#F6F7F8`: secondary panels.
- Ink `#10203E`: primary text.
- Slate `#5B6980`: explanations.
- Rule `#D7DCE4`: tables and borders.
- Red, amber, and green may appear only in explicit risk-state fields; color must never replace a written impact or residual-risk rating.

## Typography

Use `Georgia`, `Source Serif 4`, or a comparable formal serif for titles, proposal statements, and major commercial values. Use `Inter`, `Aptos`, or `Arial` for evidence. Use `IBM Plex Mono` or `Consolas` for RFP IDs, stages, certifications, SLA labels, and footer references. Cover title `54–68 px`; body title `34–44 px`; KPI `44–60 px`; card title `20–27 px`; body `13–17 px`; traceability label `10–12 px`.

## Page archetypes

### 1. Cover and confidential bid context

Use a navy-white split with a gold brand block. Include bidder, client, RFP reference, oral-defense stage, industry or scope, submission version, date, contact, confidentiality, and evaluation domains. Do not claim compliance or approval until verified.

### 2. RFP requirements and response mapping

Use three requirement cards. Each shows exact requirement ID and paraphrase, proposed response, compliance state, evidence reference, assumption or exception, and accountable solution owner. Preserve traceability to the written response.

### 3. Solution architecture and value moat

Explain the proposed delivery engine or architecture in two to four components and pair it with two evidence-backed differentiators. Identify client dependencies, third parties, optional elements, and deviations. Certifications must be current and within scope.

### 4. Execution plan, governance, and team

Use a dated phased plan with gates, acceptance evidence, dependencies, and transition controls. Pair it with governance forums and named key personnel, roles, availability, relevant credentials, and substitution rules. Distinguish proposed from committed staff.

### 5. Risk mitigation and quality assurance

Use a traceable table with risk, cause, impact, likelihood, proactive mitigation, contingency, owner, trigger, and residual risk. Include quality, security, migration, service continuity, incumbent transition, and data risks where relevant. Residual risk cannot automatically be low.

### 6. Commercial value and service commitments

Show the few evaluator-relevant financial and performance outcomes with calculation basis, then a dark commitment band for SLA, schedule, security, service credits, liability, and implementation responsibilities. State assumptions, exclusions, contract hierarchy, and validity.

## Bid integrity

Never invent certifications, references, personnel, availability, processing capacity, SLA, cost savings, payback, liability, or customer approval. Every claim must trace to a proposal section, evidence artifact, or authorized commitment. Reconcile oral defense with the submitted bid and identify any clarification or deviation. Legal and commercial guarantees require approval by authorized owners.

## Avoid

Do not use vague superiority claims, generic capability lists, unverified competitor comparisons, decorative seals, or fake compliance percentages. Do not imply an SLA, security certification, named person, timeline, or price is binding unless it is authorized and consistent with the written offer.
